_note: Plain-language career-field guide written for cadets. It complements the official AFSC descriptions from 'Air Force AFSC data.pdf'. Training pipelines and bases change, so the agent tells cadets to confirm details with their AOC, career-field managers, and AFPC.

92T0.overview: Fly Air Force aircraft - fighters, bombers, tankers, airlift, special operations, rescue, or ISR platforms - and lead aircrews.
92T0.training: Initial Flight Training (Pueblo, CO), then Undergraduate Pilot Training at Columbus, Laughlin, Vance, or Sheppard (ENJJPT), then aircraft-specific Formal Training Unit. Roughly 2 years before your first operational squadron. 10-year service commitment after wings.
92T0.lifestyle: Long training pipeline, then a flying squadron with deployments and TDYs. Strong squadron culture.
92T0.good_fit: Loves flying, handles pressure, comfortable with a long commitment.

92T1.overview: Combat Systems Officers run weapons, navigation, and electronic warfare on aircraft such as the B-1, B-52, F-15E, AC-130J, MC-130J, RC-135, and EC-130H.
92T1.training: Initial Flight Training, then Undergraduate CSO Training at NAS Pensacola, FL, then the aircraft Formal Training Unit. 6-year commitment after wings.
92T1.lifestyle: Flying squadron life with deployments; many CSOs become aircraft commanders and mission planners.
92T1.good_fit: Wants to fly and loves tactics, systems, and weapons employment.

92T2.overview: Air Battle Managers direct the air war - controlling fighters, tankers, and ISR from the E-3 AWACS, E-7, or ground control centers.
92T2.training: Initial Flight Training, then Undergraduate ABM Training at Tyndall AFB, FL, then platform training.
92T2.lifestyle: Aircrew lifestyle with deployments; big-picture command-and-control mindset.
92T2.good_fit: Multitasker who likes seeing the whole battlespace and making fast decisions.

92T3.overview: RPA pilots fly the MQ-9 Reaper and RQ-4 Global Hawk on real-world ISR and strike missions, often from the US.
92T3.training: Initial Flight Training, then RPA Instrument Qualification at JBSA-Randolph, then Formal Training Unit at Holloman or March ARB. 6-year commitment.
92T3.lifestyle: Real combat missions while living at home; shift work around the clock.
92T3.good_fit: Wants direct mission impact and to fly without the long manned-aircraft pipeline.

13C1.overview: Special Tactics Officers lead combat controllers and special reconnaissance teams who seize airfields and call in airpower alongside SOF partners.
13C1.training: Multi-phase assessment and selection, then a 2+ year pipeline (dive, airborne, freefall, SERE, Special Tactics training). Highly selective.
13C1.lifestyle: Elite special operations tempo with frequent deployments and very high physical standards.
13C1.good_fit: Athletic, mission-driven leaders who thrive in small teams - lots of athletes fit here.

13D1.overview: Combat Rescue Officers lead Pararescue (PJ) and SERE teams on personnel recovery missions so that others may live.
13D1.training: Assessment and selection, then 18+ months of training (dive, airborne, freefall, SERE, Pararescue/CRO course at Kirtland).
13D1.lifestyle: Demanding, high-ops-tempo ground and air rescue mission.
13D1.good_fit: Physically elite leaders who want a lifesaving combat mission.

13L1.overview: Air Liaison Officers embed with Army units and lead Tactical Air Control Party (TACP) Airmen to control close air support.
13L1.training: Selection, then ALO Qualification Course at JBSA-Lackland and JTAC training.
13L1.lifestyle: Live and deploy with the Army; rugged field environment.
13L1.good_fit: Wants a ground combat role connecting airpower to soldiers.

13M1.overview: Airfield Operations officers run air traffic control, airfield management, and flight operations at bases worldwide.
13M1.training: Airfield Operations officer course at Keesler AFB, MS.
13M1.lifestyle: Steady base-level leadership with some deployments.
13M1.good_fit: Detail-oriented leader who likes aviation without being aircrew.

13N1.overview: Nuclear and Missile Operations officers stand alert in launch control centers commanding Minuteman III ICBMs (and soon Sentinel).
13N1.training: Undergraduate Missile Training at Vandenberg SFB, CA, then initial qualification at your missile wing.
13N1.lifestyle: Alert rotations (24+ hour shifts) with predictable schedules; strong path to grad school and staff jobs.
13N1.good_fit: Responsible, precise, and wants the nation's most serious mission.

13S1.overview: Space Operations officers fly satellites, run missile warning, space domain awareness, and launch. Most now commission into the US Space Force.
13S1.training: Undergraduate Space Training at Vandenberg SFB, CA, then unit qualification.
13S1.lifestyle: Shift work early on, then staff, acquisition, and operations roles; a growing service.
13S1.good_fit: Tech-minded, interested in space, orbital mechanics, and a new service.

14N1.overview: Intelligence officers analyze adversaries, brief aircrews and commanders, and run targeting and ISR operations.
14N1.training: Intelligence Officer Initial Skills course at Goodfellow AFB, TX (about 7 months).
14N1.lifestyle: Office and classified environments; deployable; strong civilian crossover.
14N1.good_fit: Curious, analytical, strong writer and briefer.

15W1.overview: Weather officers forecast terrestrial and space weather for air, ground, and space operations.
15W1.training: Weather officer course at Keesler AFB, MS (often after a meteorology-heavy degree).
15W1.lifestyle: Steady schedule with field support to Army and special operations units.
15W1.good_fit: Science-minded cadets who love meteorology and data.

17D1.overview: Cyberspace Operations officers defend networks, lead cyber protection teams, and run comm systems.
17D1.training: Undergraduate Cyber Training at Keesler AFB, MS (about 6 months).
17D1.lifestyle: Office and operations-floor work with strong civilian tech crossover.
17D1.good_fit: Computer science and engineering majors who like defense and tech.

21A1.overview: Aircraft Maintenance officers lead hundreds of Airmen who generate sorties and keep aircraft flying.
21A1.training: Aircraft Maintenance Officer Course at Sheppard AFB, TX.
21A1.lifestyle: Flightline leadership with long hours; early command of large teams.
21A1.good_fit: Wants to lead big teams early and work hands-on with aircraft.

21M1.overview: Munitions and Missile Maintenance officers manage conventional munitions, nuclear weapons, and ICBM maintenance.
21M1.training: Munitions and Missile Maintenance Officer Course at Sheppard AFB, TX.
21M1.lifestyle: Leadership-heavy maintenance environment with exacting standards.
21M1.good_fit: Detail-focused leader interested in weapons and the nuclear enterprise.

21R1.overview: Logistics Readiness officers run supply, fuels, vehicles, aerial ports, and deployment planning.
21R1.training: Logistics Readiness Officer course at JB Langley-Eustis / Fort Lee.
21R1.lifestyle: Broad leadership roles; strong civilian supply-chain crossover.
21R1.good_fit: Organized problem-solvers interested in supply chains and planning.

31P1.overview: Security Forces officers lead base defense, law enforcement, and nuclear security forces.
31P1.training: Security Forces Officer Course at JBSA-Lackland, TX.
31P1.lifestyle: Shift work and early leadership of large flights; deployable.
31P1.good_fit: Leaders who want people-heavy, protective missions and law enforcement.

32E1C.overview: Civil Engineer officers build and maintain base infrastructure and lead fire, EOD, and emergency management.
32E1C.training: Civil Engineer officer courses at Wright-Patterson (AFIT) and Sheppard; engineering degree required.
32E1C.lifestyle: Project management with contingency and RED HORSE deployment options.
32E1C.good_fit: Civil, mechanical, electrical, or environmental engineering majors.

32E1G.overview: General Civil Engineers manage facility projects and programs across engineering disciplines.
32E1G.training: Civil Engineer officer courses; engineering degree required.
32E1G.good_fit: Engineering majors who want to lead projects and people.

35P1.overview: Public Affairs officers tell the Air Force story - media relations, community engagement, and strategic communication.
35P1.training: Public Affairs Qualification Course at Fort Meade, MD.
35P1.lifestyle: Fast-paced communications work close to senior leaders.
35P1.good_fit: Strong writers and speakers interested in media and communication.

38P1.overview: Force Support officers run personnel, manpower, fitness, lodging, dining, and family programs.
38P1.training: Force Support Officer course at Keesler AFB, MS.
38P1.lifestyle: People-focused leadership with a broad portfolio.
38P1.good_fit: Leaders who enjoy HR, business operations, and taking care of Airmen.

41A1.overview: Health Services Administrators run the business side of military medicine - hospital operations, budgets, and aeromedical evacuation.
41A1.training: Health Services Administration course at JBSA-Fort Sam Houston, TX.
typical_bases: Joint Base San Antonio-Fort Sam Houston, TX
41A1.lifestyle: Hospital and clinic leadership; strong civilian healthcare-management crossover.
41A1.good_fit: Interested in healthcare without being a clinician.

43A1.overview: Aerospace and Operational Physiologists train aircrew on altitude, G-forces, spatial disorientation, and human performance.
43A1.training: Aerospace and Operational Physiology course at Wright-Patterson AFB, OH.
typical_bases: Joint Base San Antonio-Fort Sam Houston, TX
43A1.lifestyle: Teaching and research with flying-adjacent work.
43A1.good_fit: Biology and human-performance majors who love aviation.

61A1.overview: Operations Research Analysts use math, statistics, and modeling to inform decisions from tactics to budgets.
61A1.training: On-the-job plus AFIT courses; strong math or OR degree.
61A1.lifestyle: Analytic office work with frequent grad-school opportunities.
61A1.good_fit: Math, data science, and OR majors.

61B1.overview: Behavioral Scientists study human performance, selection, and decision-making to improve the force.

61C1.overview: Chemists and Nuclear Chemists work on materials, propellants, and nuclear treaty monitoring.
61C1.training: Research and lab assignments; chemistry degree.
61C1.good_fit: Chemistry majors who want hands-on science.

61D1.overview: Physicists and Nuclear Engineers work on directed energy, space, nuclear effects, and test programs.
61D1.training: Research assignments; physics or nuclear engineering degree.
61D1.lifestyle: Cutting-edge research labs and test centers.

62E1A.overview: Aeronautical Engineers design, test, and modify aircraft and propulsion systems.
62E1A.training: On-the-job at program offices, labs, and test centers.
62E1A.lifestyle: Engineering office and test-range work; path to Test Pilot School as a flight test engineer.

62E1B.overview: Astronautical Engineers develop satellites, launch vehicles, and space systems.
62E1B.training: On-the-job at Space Systems Command and labs.
62E1B.lifestyle: Program office and lab work with heavy industry interaction.

62E1C.overview: Computer Systems Engineers build software, AI, and embedded systems for weapons and space programs.
62E1C.training: On-the-job at program offices and labs.
62E1C.lifestyle: Engineering office work with strong civilian tech crossover.

62E1E.overview: Electrical Engineers work on avionics, sensors, radar, and electronic warfare.
62E1E.training: On-the-job at program offices and labs.

62E1G.overview: Project Engineers manage technical programs across engineering disciplines.
62E1G.lifestyle: Program management with an engineering focus.
62E1G.good_fit: Engineering majors who enjoy leading projects.

62E1H.overview: Mechanical Engineers work on structures, propulsion, and thermal systems.
62E1H.training: On-the-job at program offices, depots, and labs.

63A1.overview: Acquisition Managers lead programs that buy and field aircraft, satellites, weapons, and software.
63A1.training: Acquisition fundamentals and on-the-job program office work.
63A1.lifestyle: Program office work with budgets, contracts, and industry; strong civilian defense-industry crossover.
63A1.good_fit: Business, management, or technical majors who like leading programs.

64P1.overview: Contracting officers negotiate and manage the contracts that buy everything from base services to fighter jets.
64P1.training: Contracting officer course at Wright-Patterson AFB, OH.
64P1.lifestyle: Business-focused office work with warranted authority.
64P1.good_fit: Business, economics, and management majors who like negotiation.

71S1.overview: Special Investigations (AFOSI) special agents investigate felony crimes, fraud, and counterintelligence threats.
71S1.training: Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (Glynco, GA) and the OSI Academy.
71S1.lifestyle: Plainclothes investigative work with irregular hours.
71S1.good_fit: Inquisitive cadets interested in law enforcement and counterintelligence.
